neighbours.label: ' the' after 'on' or 'upon' introducing a physical surface something rests on, not an abstract 'on the economy'
fire: The keys were sitting on the counter beside the mail.
An old dog lay on the porch in the afternoon sun.
At sunset we rested on the cliff above the bay.
Two gulls were perched on the roof of the boathouse.
The bottle had washed up on the sand after the storm.
Her coat was draped on the chair by the window.
They pitched their tents upon the hillside near a stream.
Les chaussures sont restées sur la table toute la journée.
quiet: The keys were in my bag, along with the mail.
She wrote an essay on the history of trade.
At sunset we paid the bill and left the bay.
The committee will vote on the budget next week.
He read the report and called the boathouse.
Her coat was bought from the shop by the station.
They agreed on the price and signed the papers.
Elle a parlé sur la politique étrangère toute la journée.

notes: Probes: 'on the' with a physical surface 0.30-0.56 (French 'sur la' 0.55), 'a talk on the economy' 0.02, object 'ate the' 0.01. It is not about coasts: 'on the table' fired as well as 'on the shore'. The card's other trigger, the word piece 'con' (0.27-0.55), is left out of this test, so the label is partial.
